question: Which of the following drug is contraindicated in a patient of myasthenia gravis: September 2008
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Succinylcholine" -> "depolarizing neuromuscular blocker" -> "exacerbates muscle weakness" -> "contraindicated in myasthenia gravis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Tubocurare" -> "non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocker" -> "increased muscle weakness" -> "contraindicated in myasthenia gravis" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Pyridostigmine" -> "acetylcholinesterase inhibitor" -> "improves neuromuscular transmission" -> "used in myasthenia gravis" -> "not contraindicated" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Halothane" -> "general anesthetic" -> "no direct effect on neuromuscular junction" -> "not contraindicated in myasthenia gravis" -> 80%
analysis: Succinylcholine is a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker that can exacerbate muscle weakness in patients with myasthenia gravis due to their already compromised neuromuscular transmission. Tubocurare, a non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocker, is also contraindicated as it can cause prolonged paralysis in these patients. Pyridostigmine is used to treat myasthenia gravis, and halothane, an anesthetic, does not have a direct contraindication in myasthenia gravis. However, among the options, succinylcholine is more commonly recognized as contraindicated due to its potential to cause severe muscle weakness and respiratory failure in myasthenic patients.
